[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested plant-based protein sources for athletes include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Soy products like tofu, tempeh, and edamame  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Legumes like chickpeas, lentils, and beans  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Nuts and seeds like almonds, peanuts, pumpkin seeds, and chia seeds  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Quinoa, a grain that is a complete protein  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Hemp seeds, which are high in protein and omega-3 fatty acids  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Seitan, a protein-rich wheat gluten  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Spirulina, a blue-green algae that is high in protein and nutrients  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Nutritional yeast, a food that is high in protein and often used in vegan dishes as a cheese substitute  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Amaranth, a grain that is high in protein and fiber  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Pea protein powder, a supplement made from yellow peas that is high in protein and easy to use as a post-workout recovery drink or shake.  
[USER] User requested quick and easy recipe ideas using plant-based protein sources.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested quick and easy recipe ideas include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Tofu scramble: Sauté crumbled tofu with veggies, turmeric, and nutritional yeast; serve with whole-grain toast.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Chickpea salad: Mash chickpeas with avocado and chopped veggies; serve on a whole-grain wrap or salad greens.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Lentil soup: Sauté onion, carrots, and garlic; add lentils, veggie broth, and canned tomatoes; simmer and serve with whole-grain bread.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Peanut butter and banana protein smoothie: Blend peanut butter, banana, almond milk, and plant-based protein powder.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Quinoa bowl: Cook quinoa and top with roasted veggies, chickpeas or tofu, and dressing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Chia seed pudding: Mix chia seeds with almond milk and sweetener; let sit overnight and serve with fruit and nuts.
